key_insight: Matrix-free fast diagonalization and tailored preconditioners reduce iteration counts and per-iteration costs for high-order finite element elliptic problems on distributed GPUs.
engineering_relevance: These solvers can accelerate large elliptic finite element analyses while supporting NVIDIA, AMD and Intel GPUs through CUDA, HIP and SYCL.
method: Distributed direct fast diagonalization provides exact solves for supported tensor-product meshes and an exact coarse solver.
Hybrid Schwarz uses fast-diagonalization cell inverses, while p-multigrid applies fused Chebyshev–Jacobi smoothing with hanging-node constraints.
FP64 conjugate gradients combine eligible FP32 operations, adaptive coarse-level distribution and multiple-right-hand-side block solves.
evidence_signal: Across mesh and coefficient tests plus four applications, the direct solver was 100–1,000× faster than Jacobi PCG on uniform meshes, and HS-FD converged in 11 iterations on an octree problem across 8–1,024 MI250X graphics compute dies.
watch_item: Direct-solver exactness requires supported tensor-product structure and coefficient variation; FP32 eligibility also depends on cell shapes and coefficients.
paper_title: Accelerating matrix-free fast diagonalization and preconditioned linear solvers for higher-order finite element discretized elliptic problems on distributed GPUs
